title: Stability of a simple root under coefficient perturbation over a henselian valued field
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial valuation and henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Its valuation topology has balls $v(x-a)>\gamma$ as a basis, for the additive valuation into a totally ordered abelian group. Let $f(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}c_iT^i\in F[T]$ be monic of degree $n\geq1$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Suppose $a\in F$ is a simple root: $f(a)=0$ and $f^{\prime}(a)\ne0$, where $f^{\prime}$ is the formal derivative. For every open neighbourhood $U$ of $a$ there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $(c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1})$ in the product topology on $F^n$ such that, for every $(d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1})\in V$, the polynomial $g(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}d_iT^i$ has a simple root $b\in U$. The valuation may have arbitrary rank; completeness is not assumed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: If F has discrete topology, so does F^(Fin n), since Fin n is finite. Take V={c} and b=a; all three assertions are the original hypotheses.

proof.text: Otherwise apply [lem-per-simple-root-perturbation-normalization] to the given ball basis, f, a and U. Obtain V,s,t and, for each d in V, an integral H with Hbar=X, g(a+sX)=tH, and the inclusion a+s*m subset U. This step uses no henselianity.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-henselian-residue-X-root] to the henselian valuation subring and H. It gives z in its maximal ideal with H(z)=0 and H prime(z) a unit.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: Set b=a+s*z. The maximal-ideal inclusion puts b in U. Apply evaluation at z to g.comp(C(a)+C(s)*X)=C(t)*H; the mapped root equality H(z)=0 yields g(b)=0. Apply formal differentiation and then evaluation to the same identity to get s*g prime(b)=t*H prime(z). The image of H prime(z), being a unit, is nonzero in the field. As t is nonzero, the right side is nonzero; hence g prime(b) is nonzero.

lean.note: Uses Mathlib AddValuation with the explicitly stated ambient-value ball basis, rather than Valued (whose topology uses the actual value group). The finite elements of Γ form the additive ordered group and ⊤ is the valuation of zero. Henselianity is imposed on the canonical valuation subring, not on the field.
